 JUDGMENT This petition is filed by the petitioner U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against respondents for seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.
02.

sentences.text:
The brief facts of case of the petitioner is that:
On 30.04.2024 at about 10.00 p.m, the petitioner was riding his Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-02-HF-6362 on Kunigal - Nelamangala NH-75 Road towards his native place,
carefully and cautiously, when he (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.3670/2024 reached near Facipic Granite, Bhavikere

, at that time, all of a sudden, a Lorry bearing No.TN-77-K-7196 being driven by its driver, in a rash and negligent manner, with high speed, which was going in front of the petitioner's Motor Cycle suddenly stopped the lorry without giving any indications.

Due to impact, the petitioner Motor Cycle dashed to the rear portion of the said lorry and he fell down and sustained grievous injuries and immediately after the accident he was shifted to Government hospital,
Nelamangala for first aid.
Later he was shifted to Manasvi hospital, for better treatment.
Later he was shifted to Aditya Orthopaedic and Trauma Centre for better treatment.

X-rays taken confirms fracture both bones left leg proximal third and fracture dislocation left elbow and underwent open reduction internal fixation for both the fractures and he was in the hospital as an inpatient from 06.05.2024 to 16.05.2024 and after discharge from the hospital till today he is taking treatment as an outpatient and he has spent Rs.2,50,000/- towards treatment, medicines,
conveyance and nourishment charges and prior to the accident the petitioner was hale and healthy and was aged about 40 years and was working as a Helper in a private factory and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
Due to accidental injuries, he is (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.3670/2024 unable to attend to his work and sustained loss of income.

The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending Lorry driver and in this regard the Nelamangala Traffic Police have registered a case against the driver of the said offending lorry.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the said offending vehicle,
are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.12,00,000/- to the petitioner together with cost and interest.
03. On service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared before the tribunal through their counsels and filed objections.

04. The respondent No.1 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioner and further denied alleged accident, negligence of the driver of offending lorry, involvement of lorry in the alleged accident, age, avocation, income of the petitioner, nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner and further denied issuance of policy in favour of respondent No.2 in respect of Lorry bearing No.TN-77-K-7196 and its validity since it is not been Rajesh B R vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126538532/
2 confirmed by the concerned policy issuing office.

5 M.V.C.No.3670/2024 policy

. The petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties and contended that the respondent No.2 had been willfully entrusted his vehicle to a person who did not possess valid and effective driving licence to drive the same as on the date of accident.

Similarly the respondent No.2 allowed to ply his vehicle on the road without having valid and effective permit and fitness certificate and hence there is breach of terms and conditions of the policy and violation of M.V. Act and the compensation claimed is highly excessive, exorbitant and hence, pray for dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.1.
05.

The respondent No.2 in his objections has denied the entire case of the petitioner and further denied alleged accident, negligence of the driver of offending lorry, involvement of lorry in the alleged accident, age, avocation, income of the petitioner, nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner and admits that he is the owner of the Lorry bearing No.TN-77-K-7196 and has got insurance policy in the respondent No.1 company to his vehicle and policy was in active and the lorry driver is having valid driving licence and contended that there is no rash and negligent driving by the lorry in causing the accident and it is due to the (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.3670/2024 negligence on the part of the petitioner who was riding his vehicle in rash and negligent manner and caused accident.

The compensation claimed is very exaggerated and hence, pray for dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.2.
06.

Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following Issues have been framed by my learned predecessor: -
ISSUES 01.

Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 30.04.2024 at about 10.00 p.m, on Kunigal - Nelamangala NH-75 Road, near Facipic Granite, Bhavikere, Kunigal, due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Lorry bearing registration No.TN-77-K-7196 as alleged in the petition?
02. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
03. What Order or Award?
07. In order to prove his case, petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and got examined doctor as PW.2 and got marked 12 documents as Ex.P.1 to 12 and closed his side evidence.
08. By way of rebuttal, the respondent No.1 got examined its Manager Legal - Claims as RW.1 and got (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.3670/2024 marked 2 documents as Ex.R.1 and 2 and closed its side evidence.

sentences.text: 09. Heard both sides.

10. My findings on the above Issues are as under:-
 Issue No.1 In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3

As per final order  for the following:
 REASONS 11. Issue No.1:- The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and in his chief-examination evidence he has reiterated the petition averments therein.

Though he has been elaborately cross-examined by the respondent No.1 counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioner that due to rash and negligent driving of the offending Lorry by its driver, the accident took place and petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
On perusal of the documents, Ex.P.1 is the FIR registered at Nelamangala Traffic Police against driver of the offending Lorry.

Ex.P.2 is Complaint shows due to rash and negligent driving of (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.3670/2024 the offending Lorry the accident was occurred and due to which the petitioner fell down and sustained injuries.
Ex.P.3 is Spot Mahazar showing the place of accident on Kunigal - Nelamangala NH-75 Road, near Facipic Granite Factory, Bhavikere, Kunigal, which is not disputed.
Ex.P.4 is IMV report which discloses that both vehicles are involved in the accident and Motor Cycle of petitioner got damaged at its front side.

Ex.P.5 is Charge sheet shows after completion the Investigation Officer has filed Charge sheet against driver of Lorry for the offences punishable U/Sec 279, 338 of IPC and Sec.122 and 187 of IMV Act for the reasons the driver of lorry without giving any indication or signal parking the lorry negligently in causing the accident.
Ex.P.6 is Wound certificate which shows that petitioner sustained 1) Fracture left tibial condyle and 2) Fracture D/L left elbow and doctor has opined that said injuries are grievous in nature.
Ex.P.7 is Discharge summary shows that the petitioner sustained fracture both bone left leg proximal third and fracture dislocation left elbow.

The oral and documentary evidence adduced by the petitioner clearly goes to show that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.3670/2024 the Lorry.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:- This Issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Road Traffic Accident.

Petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was hale and healthy and was aged about 40 years and was working as a Helper in a private company and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m and he has spent Rs.2,50,000/- towards treatment, medicines, conveyance and nourishment charges.

Due to accidental injuries, he is unable to do his work and sustained loss of Rajesh B R vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126538532/
4 income and become permanent disabled.

sentences.text: 13. So far as avocation and income of the petitioner is concerned, the petitioner has not placed any documents or evidence before the tribunal.

Therefore, in the absence of authenticated, believable and satisfactory documents regarding proof of income of the injured, this tribunal has to go by the Lok-Adalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the accident of the year 2024 to be taken as Rs.16,500/- p.m.

Therefore, this tribunal (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.3670/2024 assessed the monthly income of petitioner is at Rs.16,500/-.
14.

Looking to the nature of the injuries, it is the duty of petitioner to prove his age, but petitioner has not produced birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card to show his exact date of birth.
However, he has produced notarized copy of Aadhaar card at Ex.P.8.

Even though said document is not authenticated document for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of any other documents, the same can be relied upon and according to which, the date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 01.05.1983 and the alleged accident was occurred on 30.04.2024.
Therefore, considering the said document, this tribunal has assessed age of the petitioner as 41 years.

As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and others case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 41 to 45 years is '14'.
15.

sentences.text: According to the evidence of PW.2 doctor, who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability has stated in his examination-in-chief that petitioner sustained fracture both bones left leg (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.3670/2024 proximal third and fracture dislocation left elbow and he assessed permanent disability of about 32% to left lower limb, 24% to left upper limb and 22.5% to whole body disability which is permanent in nature and he has produced OPD card and X-ray as per Ex.P.11 and 12.
In his cross-examination PW.2 admits that petitioner taken treatment at Aditya Orthopedic and Trauma Centre, Tumakuru and he has not treated the petitioner personally at any stage.

entities.text: Aditya Orthopedic and Trauma Centre, Tumakuru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He has taken recent x-rays for both upper limb and lower limb.
As per X-ray report both fractures are united.
There is no complications at both fractures site.
There is no bone loss and loss of muscle power.
There is no shortening of both limbs.

Implants are removed at upper limb but lower limb implants are in-situ and admits that it will not cause any impact due to present condition of the patient and that hip and ankle movements are normal in lower limb.
Nearly 30 degree is restricted and shoulder joint and wrist joint of upper limb are normal.

There is loss of 20 degree and denied to the suggestion that to help the petitioner instead of taking 1/3 disability to the whole body he has taken  and admits that he has assessed physical disability and not functional disability.
He has not given estimation for removal of implants for Rs.20,000/- and denied to (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.3670/2024 the suggestion that Rs.20,000/- is not required for removal of implants.
However, considering the evidence of PW.2 and nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and medical records, this tribunal has assessed functional disability of the petitioner at 15%.

Therefore,
the loss of future income works out as under:
Rs.16,500/- x 12 x 14 x 15/100 = Rs.4,15,800/-.

sentences.text: Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:- As per Ex.P.7 Discharge summary of Aditya Orthopaedic and Trauma Centre, Tumakuru, wherein he took treatment as inpatient for 11 days.

sentences.text: During the aforesaid period, the petitioner might have spent a considerable amount towards attendant charges, special diet, transportation and nutrition.

Therefore,
considering the duration of treatment, towards attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.
17. Pain and sufferings:
As per Ex.P.6 Wound certificate and as per evidence of PW.2 Doctor and as per X-ray and on account of accidental injuries, petitioner has undergone pain and agony.
Accordingly with regard to grievous injuries suffered by him in the (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.3670/2024 accident, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.
18. Loss of income during laid up period:-
As already discussed above, the petitioner has not produced any documents regarding his income.
This tribunal has assessed the income of Rs.16,500/- per month and he was admitted in the hospital for 11 days as inpatient.
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment taken, duration of his stay in hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least two months.
Thus, taking into account the income of the petitioner, this tribunal award a sum of Rs.33,000/- (Rs.16,500/- x 2) under this head.
19. Medical Expenses:- The petitioner has got marked entire Medical bills as per Ex.P.9 and 10 for Rs.1,27,649/- and Rs.40,350/-.
To disprove the medical bills, the respondents have not produced any documents nor any evidence.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,67,999/- under this head.
20. Loss of future amenities and unhappiness:-

Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness, the claimant has to undergo in his future life, it is just (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.3670/2024 and proper to award a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards future loss of amenities and unhappiness.
21. Future medical expenses:-
According to doctor PW.2 the petitioner needs surgery for removal of implants which may costs around Rs.20,000/- in their hospital.
But he has not produced any estimation regarding future medical expenses.

Hence, under the facts and circumstances of the case,
the petitioner is entitled for Rs.15,000/- under this head.
22. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-

Sl. Head of compensation Amount in No. Rs.
1. Loss of future income 4,15,800-00 2.
Pain and Sufferings 30,000-00 3.
Attendant charges, extra 30,000-00  nutritious food and conveyance  charges 4.

Medical Expenses 1,67,999-00 5. Loss of future amenities and 30,000-00 Rajesh B R vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126538532/
6  unhappiness 6. Loss of income during laid up 33,000-00  period 7. Future medical expenses 15,000-00

Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.7,21,799/- with (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.3670/2024 interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.15,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.

24. Regarding liability:- To disprove the case of the petitioner, the respondent No.1 got examined its Manager - Legal Claims as RW.1 and in his chief-examination evidence he has deposed that this respondent has issued policy in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of Lorry bearing No.TN-77-K-7196 and it is valid as on the date of accident.
Further, he has produced Ex.R.2 copy of Policy pertaining to offending Lorry which shows that the policy is valid and is in force as on the date of accident.
In his cross-examination he stated that based on the documents, they know how the accident happened.
The final report was never questioned.
The driver had a driving license and insurance at the time of the accident.
Therefore, this tribunal is of the considered opinion that, as on the date of accident there is no breach of any fundamental terms and conditions of the insurance policy by the respondent No.2.
As such, it appears that as on the date of accident the insurance policy of the offending Lorry was valid and is in force.

Therefore, under the above facts and circumstances of the case, this tribunal is the opinion that, the (SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.3670/2024 respondent No.1 being the insurer and respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending Lorry are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

However, since insurance policy of the offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 being the insurer shall pay above said compensation amount to the petitioner.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.
25. Issue No.3:

In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.7,21,799/- (Rupees Seven lakhs twenty one thousand seven hundred and ninety nine only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.15,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, the petitioner is entitled to get release 70% of the award amount through E-payment directly to the petitioner account by obtaining the bank account details Rajesh B R vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126538532/
7 and remaining 30% shall be kept in fixed deposit in any scheduled bank for a period of three years, in his name.
